LIVE COMPARISON

Official Winter requires exactly one purchased machine and one rented premise. Invalid production or allocation is flagged, not silently changed. Requests and trainer allocations use 10,000-unit blocks. Milk and unsold output spoil at season end.

04 What changes between the plans?

DOWNSIDE CHECK

When allocation falls short

Reduce each plan’s allocation by this percentage, then round down to a 10,000-unit block. A 20% cut to 60,000 therefore tests 40,000 sales. Production and advance costs stay locked; transport, bonus and tax adjust. No sales advance is received.

05 Accounting method and decision record

The official profit statement

Revenue − full milk cost − all machine maintenance − depreciation = gross profit. Deduct transport, market investment, positive-gross-profit bonus, fixed salaries, rent and interest to get profit before tax. Deduct game tax to get net profit.

Post each monetary line in whole shekels, then build subtotals from those posted lines. This tool rounds half-shekels upward. Milk is expensed once; there is no second spoilage expense.

Cash timing is different

Start with Sh 100,000 plus the loan. Pay the machine, milk and market investment in advance. No customer advance exists in these rules. Sales receipts, rent, maintenance, transport, salaries, bonus, bank payments and tax are season-end items.

Check cash after each advance and at season end. Net cash flow = net profit + depreciation − machine purchase + borrowing − principal repayment. No extra intra-day order is assumed for season-end items.

Assets, loans and tax losses

A new machine is depreciated over eight seasons; seven remain after Winter. Maintenance and depreciation continue even when idle. A new loan has a 1–8 season term, first principal repayment immediately this season, and 10% interest before repayment. Outstanding debt before repayment cannot exceed Sh 200,000.

Principal equals loan / term, posted to whole shekels. Fractional installment rounding should be reconciled in the final installment. This first-Winter tool starts with zero carried tax loss. A current loss creates a pool; no refund is received. Later-season losses and loan schedules require a separate rolling ledger.

Before you lock decisions

Record the chosen premise, machine, milk, production, market spend, eligible sales request and loan. Print this comparison and identify the chosen plan. The allocation field is a scenario until the trainer reports the real result; update it afterward.

Recommended starting plan: Machine 1, Premise D, three tons of milk, 60,000 produced and requested, Sh 1,000 market investment and no loan. Do not spend the Sh 4,000 advance-payment buffer without checking liquidity. The market ranking and rivals’ decisions are unknown; this is not a guaranteed winning bid.
